raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Adds a `pinned_staging` key to the Run:ai streamer loader's `--model-loader-extra-config`. When set, the streamer's CPU staging buffer is page-locked once per load and the streamer copies every tensor to the device out of it, so the weight loaders only see device tensors and the host-to-device traffic is DMA out of pinned memory rather than pageable memcpy. Off by default; nothing changes when the key is unset.

## Claims

- On a copy-bound load, the model-loading stage gets substantially faster. Measured on vLLM **0.20.2** (this PR is the port to `main`, see Validation): GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (433 GiB, 232k tensors) as four TP=2 replicas on an 8xB300, `"Model loading took"` 75–79 s → 39–42 s (−48 %), four replicas serving at 133 s instead of 170 s from script start.
- Weights are bit-identical to the stock loader (every GPU parameter hashed after `process_weights_after_loading` on both paths), and throughput is unchanged.
- Any failure to pin (no CUDA, `cudaHostRegister` error, streamer internals changed) falls back to the existing path with a warning.

## Validation

- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/runai_streamer_loader/`: new tests for the extra-config validation, the bounded default `RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT`, and the CPU fallback of the iterator with `pinned_staging=True`; the existing buffer-reuse and loader tests still pass (13 passed locally on CPU, `--noconftest`).
- `pre-commit` `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos` pass on the changed files.
- **Not yet re-run on hardware against `main`.** The numbers above come from the same change on 0.20.2 (patch on the loader in `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py` with `runai-model-streamer` 0.16.1). Since then `main` started cloning tensors out of the streamer (#43464); on the pinned path the streamer's own `.to(device)` is that copy, so the clone is skipped there (and kept for the distributed streamer, whose device buffer is reused). I will re-measure on `main` as soon as I have the node again and post the numbers here; until then this stays a draft.

Repro of the measurement: `vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 -tp 2 --load-format runai_streamer --model-loader-extra-config '{"pinned_staging": true}'` vs. without the key, same node, same page-cache state; compare the `Model loading took` log line.

## Details

The streamer reads each tensor into one reusable pageable host buffer (`requests_iterator.buffer`), and `param.copy_()` out of it runs as a driver-staged pageable memcpy per tensor: about 2.4 GB/s per worker with eight workers on this node, 4.5 GB/s alone. With the buffer registered (`cudaHostRegister`) the copies run at about 15 GB/s per worker.

Registration of a large buffer is single-threaded and page-fault-bound, so the buffer is first faulted in with `MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` from 16 threads (and advised `MADV_HUGEPAGE`), then registered: about 0.2 s/GB, i.e. 3–4 s for the 16 GB default. Because that cost is per byte of buffer, the streamer's 40 GB default `RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT` is bounded to 16 GB when `pinned_staging` is set and the user did not set `memory_limit` (16 GB showed no streaming penalty on this model). The buffer is unregistered in a `finally` when the iterator is exhausted.

Where it does not help: at TP=8 on the same node the gain was 2–4 s on 47 s, because every rank reads the whole checkpoint through the page cache and the stage is a memcpy, not the copy path.

Stacked PR using this: the sleep-mode reload fix, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61304.

+You can set `pinned_staging` to page-lock the streamer's CPU buffer and have the streamer copy every tensor to the GPU out of it, so the host-to-device copies run as DMA copies from pinned memory instead of pageable copies. +# Default size of the Run:ai streamer's CPU staging buffer when it is
+# page-locked (``pinned_staging``). Registering the buffer costs roughly
+# 0.2 s/GB once per load; 16 GB keeps that to a few seconds while leaving the
+# streamer enough room to keep every reader busy.
+RUNAI_PINNED_STAGING_DEFAULT_BYTES = 16_000_000_000
+# Threads used to pre-fault the staging buffer before it is page-locked.
+_RUNAI_PINNED_STAGING_TOUCH_THREADS = 16
+
+
+def _pin_runai_streamer_buffer(streamer) -> int | None:
+    """Page-lock the Run:ai streamer's CPU staging buffer.
+
+    The streamer reads every tensor into one reusable host buffer and the
+    host-to-device copies out of it run as pageable copies, i.e. a driver
+    staged memcpy per tensor. Registering the buffer with ``cudaHostRegister``
+    turns those into DMA copies out of pinned memory. The pages are faulted in
+    with ``MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`` from several threads first, so the
+    single-threaded registration does not pay for the page faults itself.
+
+    Returns the registered address, to be passed to ``cudaHostUnregister``
+    once the iterator is exhausted, or ``None`` if the buffer could not be
+    pinned. In that case loading continues unchanged on the pageable path.
+    """
+    try:
+        buf = streamer.file_streamer.file_streamer.requests_iterator.buffer
+    except AttributeError as e:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Run:ai streamer staging buffer not found (%s); "
+            "loading from pageable memory.",
+            e,
+        )
+        return None
+    nbytes = int(buf.nbytes)
+    if nbytes == 0:
+        return None
+    addr = int(buf.ctypes.data)
+    start_time = time.perf_counter()
+    try:
+        import ctypes
+
+        libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6", use_errno=True)
+        page = 4096
+        madv_hugepage = 14  # MADV_HUGEPAGE
+        madv_populate_write = 23  # MADV_POPULATE_WRITE, Linux >= 5.14
+        begin = addr & ~(page - 1)
+        end = (addr + nbytes + page - 1) & ~(page - 1)
+        libc.madvise(
+            ctypes.c_void_p(begin), ctypes.c_size_t(end - begin), madv_hugepage
+        )
+        step = (end - begin) // _RUNAI_PINNED_STAGING_TOUCH_THREADS
+        step = max((step + page - 1) & ~(page - 1), page)
+
+        def _populate(lo: int, hi: int) -> None:
+            libc.madvise(
+                ctypes.c_void_p(lo), ctypes.c_size_t(hi - lo), madv_populate_write
+            )
+
+        threads = [
+            threading.Thread(target=_populate, args=(lo, min(lo + step, end)))
+            for lo in range(begin, end, step)
+        ]
+        for thread in threads:
+            thread.start()
+        for thread in threads:
+            thread.join()
+        populated_time = time.perf_counter()
+
+        rc = torch.cuda.cudart().cudaHostRegister(addr, nbytes, 0)
+        if int(rc) != 0:
+            logger.warning(
+                "cudaHostRegister on the Run:ai streamer staging buffer returned "
+                "%s; loading from pageable memory.",
+                rc,
+            )
+            return None
+        logger.info(
+            "Page-locked the %.1f GB Run:ai streamer staging buffer "
+            "(populate %.2f s, register %.2f s).",
+            nbytes / 1e9,
+            populated_time - start_time,
+            time.perf_counter() - populated_time,
+        )
+        return addr
+    except Exception as e:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not page-lock the Run:ai streamer staging buffer (%s); "
+            "loading from pageable memory.",
+            e,
+        )
+        return None
+
+
 def runai_safetensors_weights_iterator(
     hf_weights_files: list[str],
     use_tqdm_on_load: bool,

+    pinned_staging: bool = False,

+            the weight loaders only ever see device tensors. Falls back to the
+            pageable path if the buffer cannot be pinned.
+

         is_cuda_alike = current_platform.is_cuda_alike()
+        stream_to_device = is_cuda_alike and (is_distributed or pinned_staging)
         device = (
-            f"cuda:{current_platform.current_device()}"
-            if is_distributed and is_cuda_alike
-            else "cpu"
+            f"cuda:{current_platform.current_device()}" if stream_to_device else "cpu"
         )
 
         streamer.stream_files(
             hf_weights_files,
             device=device,
             is_distributed=is_distributed,
         )
+        pinned_addr = _pin_runai_streamer_buffer(streamer) if pinned_staging else None
         total_tensors = sum(
             len(tensors_meta)
             for tensors_meta in streamer.files_to_tensors_metadata.values()
@@ -1276,8 +1380,23 @@ def runai_safetensors_weights_iterator(

-            yield name, tensor.clone()

+                # The streamer reuses its staging buffers, so a tensor must be
+                # copied out before the next chunk lands in the same memory.
+                # On the pinned path (non-distributed) the streamer has already
